construct: CTSK encodes cathepsin K, a lysosomal cysteine protease highly expressed by osteoclasts. Osteoclasts in pycnodysostosis can acidify and demineralize bone, but cathepsin K deficiency markedly impairs degradation of type I collagen and other bone-matrix proteins, producing osteosclerosis with brittle bones and characteristic acroosteolysis and delayed cranial-suture closure.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Osteosclerosis with fragility, acroosteolysis, open cranial sutures, normal acid-base status, and normal osteoclast morphology identifies pycnodysostosis; CTSK loss selectively impairs collagenous matrix proteolysis after demineralization.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Failure to acidify the resorption lacuna can also cause dense brittle bone, but it conflicts with the pycnodysostosis phenotype, normal acid-base studies, and the cathepsin-K-specific preservation of demineralization.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Normal osteoclast numbers and ruffled borders plus the characteristic CTSK phenotype isolate matrix-protein degradation rather than differentiation, fusion, adhesion, or acidification.
